findings.text: follow-on: the base arm ran at revision 4d1feeed905d145a3130e71293f2cfdf1233f1d7, which is a descendant of the node's declared base 422d114dcce (git merge-base --is-ancestor 4d1feeed 422d114dc is false; the reverse is true), so the base comparison carries peer commits landed after the node's base and a failure those peers introduced would read as pre-existing here; the run discloses the head-overlay of the departure test file but not that the base revision itself moved.

item_verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit 70ddee8b..0fa80a02c: e38ca08e4 rewrites the settled branch of classify_pointer to take fleet_verdict's state, adds LedgerError to the promote guard's catch, and replaces the eager ledger reader with _LedgerRunWordReader reading per-run rows after a membership check; 82c41a5bb updates the boundary assertion to require the recorded word on both surfaces; 527998fac and 0fa80a02c extend the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: The node's done-when names tests/test_the_departure_row_says_how_and_what_it_spent.py over the departure population; the run's arms at head 82c41a5b are resume-3-exact-46-head-lowload.log (607 passed, EXIT=0) and resume-3-exact-46-base.log (6 failed, 599 passed, EXIT=1), both completed true, so added_failure_count is 0 and no failing id was added; the 4 base failures in the departure file are the node's own added cases red before the change.
item_verdicts.goal: The reviewed range settles a commitless completion under one word across classification and fleet_verdict, refuses a malformed run id as no promotion, and bounds the departure reader to the runs leaving the fleet, closing both follow-ons the prior review at 70ddee8b raised.
item_verdicts.manifest: status complete; commits through 0fa80a02c; baseline_suite revision 4d1feeed failure_count 6 and after_suite revision 82c41a5b failure_count 0, both completed true with the named logs; the malformed-id and no-commit cases pass at head and fail at base; every sha and log path quoted resolves here.
item_verdicts.write_paths: All five changed paths sit inside the declared write paths: reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_the_departure_row_says_how_and_what_it_spent.py, tests/test_crew_watch_lifetime.py, tests/test_a_promotion_never_reads_unpromoted.py and the evidence fragment; no file outside them changed in 70ddee8b..0fa80a02c.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_departure_row_says_how_and_what_it_spent.py::test_malformed_run_id_cannot_hold_a_promotion fails if the LedgerError catch is dropped and ::test_a_row_with_no_commits_cannot_claim_promotion now asserts classification==recorded==fleet_verdict.state, so both fixes redden if reverted; the negative control shows the added cases red at base source.
justifications.evidence: the exact 46-file population runs at base 4d1feeed (6 failed, 599 passed) and head 82c41a5b (607 passed, EXIT=0) with the departure file overlaid from head at base; negative-control-no-commit-and-spend.log reddens the no-commit and missing-spend ids the head passes, and the three-worker head arm's 3 failures are all pytest-timeout traces preserved in its own log.
justifications.fit: the recorded/promoted word is consistent across recovery.py FLEET_SETTLED_STATES, _recorded_pointer_word and _watch_verdict, the bounded reader keeps the existing word contract, and no changed name carries a plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: recovery.py classify_pointer now sets classification from fleet_verdict['state'] when it is in FLEET_SETTLED_STATES ({promoted, recorded}), so a commitless row reads recorded on both surfaces (reproduced at head: classification=recorded, fleet_verdict.state=recorded); the two prior follow-ons are closed.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path is inside the declared write paths and the run manifest's changed_paths, and no file outside them changed across the four commits.
